proposed_pattern: Model roasted, grilled and seared beef as one native beef core plus a high-heat transformation family, with technique/doneness-specific weighting rather than literal row-for-row equivalence.
direct_evidence_refs: SRC-BEEF-ROAST-001; SRC-BEEF-LIPIDOMICS-001; SRC-BEEF-GRILL-TEMP-001; SRC-BEEF-GRILL-GCO-001; SRC-BEEF-SEAR-001; SRC-BEEF-PANFRY-BREED-001
what_direct_evidence_supports: Across roast, grill and sear, lipid-derived aldehydes persist while heat increases Maillard/Strecker/pyrazine chemistry; grill doneness forms distinct abundance clusters; sear remains dominated by the same aldehyde backbone.
inference_boundary: Technique, surface geometry, doneness and smoke/char alter weighting and can introduce deltas. Shared architecture is not identical chemistry.
culinary_runtime_value: Allows CulinAI to reason from one high-heat mechanism while preserving technique effects.

proposed_pattern: Use a lean/native beef core plus fat/IMF-dependent abundance, release and sensory-importance weighting; add breed/cut deltas only when evidence shows material divergence.
what_direct_evidence_supports: Independent raw and grilled studies show fat/IMF changes concentration, volatile generation, in-mouth release and sensory outcome; multi-breed pan-fry data shows genuine member deltas without requiring separate total universes.
inference_boundary: Do not convert this into a fixed multiplier or assume all muscles/breeds share every compound.
culinary_runtime_value: Reduces cut proliferation while preserving the major chemical reason marbling changes flavor.

proposed_pattern: Moist-cooked beef retains a lipid-derived aldehyde/alcohol backbone while adding or emphasizing brothy/meaty sulfur and selected heterocyclic odorants.
what_direct_evidence_supports: Clean water+salt stewed beef has GC-O/AEDA aroma-active evidence overlapping raw/roast aldehydes plus methional and 2-acetyl-2-thiazoline.
inference_boundary: One stewed protocol is not every braise; headspace extraction and liquid geometry matter.
culinary_runtime_value: Supports cooked-beef core + moist-heat transformation + introduced-ingredient overlay.

proposed_pattern: Dry aging is a first-class beef transformation: oxygen exposure, proteolysis/lipolysis and microbial activity change the uncooked volatile pool and precursor availability, which then changes the grilled aroma profile. The effect is duration-dependent, not a simple monotonic intensification.
what_direct_evidence_supports: Matched dry/wet aging produces large day-28 deltas in propanal, 2-methylbutanal, 2-methylpropanal, 2-methyl-2-propanethiol and ethyl propanoate; grilled dry-aged beef shows higher concentrations/intensities of multiple desirable GC-O odorants.
inference_boundary: The optimal duration and magnitude are process-specific. One study's 35-day preference and 56-day decline must not become a universal time rule.
culinary_runtime_value: Allows CulinAI to explain dry-aged flavor as changed chemistry and precursor formation rather than a generic 'more intense beef' label.

proposed_pattern: Analytical beef occurrence must not be treated as desirable culinary aroma when the evidence context is spoilage.
what_direct_evidence_supports: 3-octanone is directly observed in minced-beef spoilage dynamics.
inference_boundary: This does not prove 3-octanone can never occur in desirable beef; this source cannot justify that claim.
culinary_runtime_value: Prevents analytically correct but culinarily harmful recommendations.

proposed_pattern: Beef fat should be modeled as a separate product/material with its own volatile inventory and preparation transformations, not as a cut label inside the muscle profile.
what_direct_evidence_supports: Dry-rendered abdominal subcutaneous fat yields 96 source-identified volatiles across aldehydes, alcohols, ketones, acids, six lactones, sulfur/nitrogen heterocycles and phenols; 54 rows have authentic-standard agreement.
inference_boundary: This source represents rendered subcutaneous fat, not intramuscular fat or every bovine fat depot.
culinary_runtime_value: Makes the carrier layer available to culinary reasoning without contaminating muscle-state inheritance.

proposed_pattern: Dry-curing with smoking/spices creates a distinct processing-derived volatile layer, especially phenols and smoke-associated cyclic ketones/furans, on top of the underlying beef/lipid profile.
what_direct_evidence_supports: The matched product comparison identifies 86 compounds; 12 phenols are found only in the smoked+spiced product, while the unsmoked/unspiced product remains dominated by lipid-derived aldehydes/alcohols.
inference_boundary: Smoking and spices co-vary in T1. The source supports a combined processing overlay more strongly than a pure smoke-only attribution for every compound.
culinary_runtime_value: Adds the phenolic processing chemistry missing from the avian-heavy dataset while preserving provenance.
